pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Scenario briefing · fictional
pages.subject: If I hadn’t gone to Toronto
paragraphs: Fictional profile: took a practical course in Toronto; later used the skills on a community project; now leads small projects with more confidence. A collaborator was met during the course. No job offer or inevitable career outcome is claimed. Alternative timelines are hypotheses, not evidence.

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: In this story, what made the short course in Toronto a turning point?
lines.audioText: In this story, what made the short course in Toronto a turning point?
lines.translation: Nesta história, o que tornou o curso curto em Toronto um ponto de virada?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: The person took a chance on a practical course and now feels confident leading small projects
lines.audioText: The person took a chance on a practical course and now feels confident leading small projects.
lines.translation: A pessoa arriscou fazer um curso prático e hoje se sente confiante para liderar projetos pequenos

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: So if they hadn’t taken the course, they wouldn’t be doing that now?
lines.audioText: So if they hadn’t taken the course, they wouldn’t be doing that now?
lines.translation: Então, se não tivesse feito o curso, não estaria fazendo isso hoje?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: They might be less confident, but we can’t know that they’d never have learned another way
lines.audioText: They might be less confident, but we can’t know that they’d never have learned another way.
lines.translation: Talvez tivesse menos confiança, mas não sabemos se nunca teria aprendido de outra forma

questions.prompt: What did the person gain from the Toronto course?
questions.answer: They now feel confident leading small projects

questions.prompt: What past decision led to that experience?
questions.answer: They took a chance on a practical course in Toronto

questions.prompt: Why can’t Kim say the person would never have learned another way?
questions.answer: The outcome of another learning route is unknown

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: That’s fair. What actually happened after the course?
lines.audioText: That’s fair. What actually happened after the course?
lines.translation: É justo. O que realmente aconteceu depois do curso?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: They used the new skills on a community project and met a future collaborator
lines.audioText: They used the new skills on a community project and met a future collaborator.
lines.translation: Usou as novas habilidades em um projeto comunitário e conheceu uma futura colaboradora

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Was meeting that person part of the original plan?
lines.audioText: Was meeting that person part of the original plan?
lines.translation: Conhecer essa pessoa fazia parte do plano original?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Not at all. That was an unexpected consequence, not a promised outcome
lines.audioText: Not at all. That was an unexpected consequence, not a promised outcome.
lines.translation: Não. Foi uma consequência inesperada, não um resultado prometido

questions.prompt: Where did the person use the new skills?
questions.answer: They used the new skills on a community project

questions.prompt: Who did they meet after the course?
Was that meeting a planned outcome?
questions.answer: No, the meeting was an unexpected consequence

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What would be different now if that meeting hadn’t happened?
lines.audioText: What would be different now if that meeting hadn’t happened?
lines.translation: O que seria diferente hoje se aquele encontro não tivesse acontecido?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: The collaboration might not exist, although they could still have developed the skills
lines.audioText: The collaboration might not exist, although they could still have developed the skills.
lines.translation: A colaboração talvez não existisse, embora ainda pudesse ter desenvolvido as habilidades

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: So the experience matters, but there isn’t only one possible path
lines.audioText: So the experience matters, but there isn’t only one possible path.
lines.translation: Então a experiência importa, mas não existe só um caminho possível

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Exactly. I’d separate the facts from what we imagine about the alternative
lines.audioText: Exactly. I’d separate the facts from what we imagine about the alternative.
lines.translation: Exatamente. Eu separaria os fatos do que imaginamos sobre a alternativa

questions.prompt: What might not exist without the meeting?
questions.answer: The collaboration might not exist without the meeting

questions.prompt: Could the person still have developed skills another way?
questions.answer: Yes, they could still have developed the skills another way

questions.prompt: What distinction does Ana want to preserve?
questions.answer: Ana separates facts from imagined alternatives

pages.title: Connect a past choice to today
pages.instruction: Take the Toronto profile as your role. Tell Teacher how the course affected you and what might be different

pages.title: Connect different times with mixed conditionals
pages.instruction: Use an unreal condition at one time to imagine a result at another

rows.subject: Past condition → result now
rows.verb: If + had + past participle, would + base verb
rows.example: If I hadn’t taken the course, I wouldn’t feel so confident now

rows.subject: Present condition → past result
rows.verb: If + past form, would have + past participle
rows.example: If I were more confident, I would have spoken at the meeting

rows.subject: A less certain result now
rows.verb: If + had + past participle, might / could + base verb
rows.example: If I’d studied elsewhere, I might work in a different team now

pages.note: Make the time relationship clear with context or words such as now. Would states the imagined result; might/could make it less certain. These are hypothetical alternatives, not proven outcomes.

pages.title: Use the information to respond
pages.instruction: Two possible paths. Explain how a past choice affects the present

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: The unexpected collaboration. Listen to both voice notes, then answer and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. There’s one more detail about that short course. The unexpected benefit wasn’t a job offer. The person met someone who later invited them to help with a community project. They still collaborate now, and that work has made it easier to explain their skills to other people
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. There’s one more detail about that short course. The unexpected benefit wasn’t a job offer. The person met someone who later invited them to help with a community project. They still collaborate now, and that work has made it easier to explain their skills to other people.
pages.greeting: There was an unexpected benefit from that course

items.prompt: Was the unexpected benefit a job offer?
items.answer: No, the person met someone who later invited them onto a community project

items.prompt: How does that collaboration still help today?
items.answer: The collaboration helps them explain their skills to others

items.prompt: Why is ‘no opportunities at all’ too strong?
items.answer: Another route might have created opportunities, although its outcome is unknown

additionalAudios.audioText: If they hadn’t gone to Toronto, that particular collaboration might not exist today. But it would be too strong to say they’d have no opportunities at all. Could you explain the present consequence and then describe a plausible alternative, making clear which part is a fact and which part is only a possibility?
